 Judgment

Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondent, asserting that on 10.01.2016 at about 11.00 a.m. when travelling by sitting in a TNSRTC bus bearing No.TN-32-N-3702 on Chennai-Pandi road, near Elanthoppan, ECR , Kanchipuram, driver of the bus drove the same negligently in a zig-zag manner dashed the same to barricade, made the bus to turn turtle, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Chiettinad hospital, Kalampappam and Vijaya hospital , Vadapalani,
Channai, as on the date of accident petitioner being aged 52 years used to earn Rs.77,000/- p.m. by working as Technician at BHEL, Bengaluru.

3. In response to the notice, respondent appeared through his Advocate, filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

4. On the basis of the pleadings on 01.03.2021, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 10.01.2016 at about 11.00 a.m. near Elanthoppan, E.C.R.
Salai, Chennai to Pandi road, Kanchipuram, Tamilnadu, within the jurisdiction of E.I.Mamallapuram police station rash and negligent driving of the T.N.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No.TN-32-N-3702 by its driver when the petitioner was travelling in the above said T.N.S.R.T.C. bus?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
5. On 18.11.2022, 01.06.2023, petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 6 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.6.
On 08.08.2023 petitioner produced the evidence of Krishnamurthy , VITA Vijaya Health Center as PW2 and get produced 3 documents at Ex.P.7 to P.9.
On 08.12.2023 respondent produced the evidence of driver of the bus as RW1.
6. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

7. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative  Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitled to Rs.1,55,000/-

As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS  8. Issues No.1 and 2 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 10.01.2016 at about 11.00 a.m. when travelling by sitting in a TNSRTC bus bearing No.TN-32-N- 3702 on Chennai-Pandi road, near Elanthoppan, ECR , Kanchipuram, driver of the bus drove the same negligently in a zig-zag manner dashed the same to barricade, made the bus to turn turtle, thereby caused the accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
9. In the written statement respondent denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
10. In the cross-examination petitioner denied the suggestion that the accident was not taken place due to the error of the driver of the bus.
11. In the evidence PW2 stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.

12. In the evidence RW1 , driver of the bus stated that on 10.01.2016, he was driving TNSRTC bus bearing No.TN-32-N-3702 from Chennai to wards Kadalur near Elanthoppan,Chennai-Pandi road,
ECR , Kanchipuram, a rider of the two wheeler rode the same negligently, suddenly crossed the road from right side, on noticing the crossing of the motorcycle , he turned the bus towards left side,
therefore, bus came in contact with the barricade, then became turn turtle, resulting in the simple injuries to a passenger.

In this case the petitioner has not cross- examined RW1.
13.

Ex.P.1 and enclosure are copy of the FIR and translated copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.7/16 registered by EI Mamalapuram police against the driver of the TNSRTC bus bearing No.TN-32-N-3702 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC,
resulting in the injuries to the petitioner/passenger on the basis of the complaint presented by N.Kalimutthu.

In this case at this stage there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident which has been supported by the evidence of RW1,
driver of the bus.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that on 10.01.2016 at about 11.00 a.m. when petitioner was travelling by sitting in a TNSRTC bus bearing No.TN-32-N-3702 on Chennai-Pandi road, near Elanthoppan, ECR , Kanchipuram, RW1, driver of the bus drove the same negligently in a zig-zag manner dashed the same to barricade, made the bus turn turtle, thereby caused the accident,
caused injuries to the petitioner/passenger.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

14. Issue No.2: In the evidence, petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered injuries to left leg, left hip, shoulder , head , took treatment at Chettinad hospital, Kalampappam , then took Rajanna M.C vs Tamilnadu State Transport Corporation ... on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95257191/
3 treatment at Vijaya hospital , N.S.K., Salai, Vadapalani, Chennai as an inpatient from 10.01.2016 to 21.01.2016 by spending Rs.2 lakhs.

sentences.text:
15. Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.76,907/-p.m. by working as Technician at BHEL Ltd., Electronic Division at Bengaluru and in view of the injuries suffered in the accident lost commuted leave, he would have earn encashment worth of Rs.1,05,273/-.
16.
In the written statement respondent denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries might have been suffered by the petitioner.
17. In the cross-examination petitioner denied the suggestion of non-spending of Rs.2,00,000/- .
Petitioner admitted that medical expenses are re-imbursed from the company and as on the date of cross-examination continued in the same job.
In the evidence PW2 and RW1 stated nothing regarding nature and consequences of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

18. Discharge summary, case file shows that in the accident petitioner suffered fracture of shaft of femur left, fracture of left scapula, head injury, concussion brain , took treatment at Vijaya hospital,
Vadapalani, Chennai as an inpatient from 10.01.2016 to 21.01.2016 at the cost of Rs.2,74,562/-
which are borne by the employer of the petitioner (BHEL).
19.
Salary certificate shows that during January 2016 petitioner being an employee at BHEL earned Rs.76,907/p.m. as gross salary , Rs.35,258/- as net salary.
In this case petitioner has not produced any type of evidence to show either loss of salary or loss of leave credit.
20. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is not entitled to receive compensation under the head of medical expenses, loss of leave credit or loss of salary during treatment period.
Hence, I award Rs.80,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.15,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.60,000/- loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
21. Therefore, I came to the conclusion that petitioner is entitle of Rs.1,55,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondent as compensation.
22. The respondent being the owner of the TNSRTC bus bearing No.TN-32-N-3702 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed .
The respondent owner of TNSRTC bus bearing No.TN- 32-N-3702 shall pay Rs.1,55,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent owner of TNSRTC bus bearing No.TN- 32-N-3702 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
